correctness.rationale: The exact Gegenbauer Laplace integral is obtained from finite parity-supported trigonometric expansions, m vanished even moments and large-a normalization; it is strictly positive for all degrees. Differentiation gives the affine slope factor. In each parity the logarithmic derivative strictly increases; a first-term lower bound proves that the global minimum is degree zero, and the unachieved global supremum is the even high-degree limit. These force and suffice for the stated two endpoints. Strict positivity on distinct sites holds because infinitely many coefficients of both degree parities remain positive at either endpoint. The coth partial fraction proves the exact all-dimensional lower limit with remainder. A high-precision numerical quadrature script checked 105 integrals to <8.6e-50 error, 35 exact polynomial identities and 1500 sign cases; numerical checks are corroboration only and do not prove infinite claims. Boundary quantifiers and exclusions are explicit.

originality.rationale: Beneath the usual bounded historical uncertainty, the inspected primary works give general Schoenberg/Pólya criteria, convolution smoothness or fixed-Matérn restrictions rather than the exact free-slope odd-sphere classification. The closest accessible in-ledger formula is restricted to S1, whose lower bound is demonstrably not sufficient on S3 and higher. Present new contribution is the dimension-dependent negative lower interval, exact all-odd-dimensional spectral inequality, strict endpoint behavior, and high-dimensional -2/pi intersection. Unindexed equivalent proofs remain possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent coefficient identity or sharp free-slope interval may have appeared in an unindexed work or appendix beyond bounded text inspection.
General Schoenberg theory provides the necessary framework; independent expert novelty confirmation has not been obtained.

value.rationale: A signed affine modification interpolates geodesic Laplace and nominal Matern 3/2 covariance, whose fixed positive slope is known to fail on spheres. The full odd-dimensional exact parameter window resolves which repairs are valid and supplies explicit negative harmonic witnesses outside both boundaries, endpoint strict interpolation behavior, a dimension-independent optimal upper slope, a dimension-dependent negative slope and its sharp -2/pi all-dimensional limit. It directly guides geodesic covariance construction and is not a textbook one-line substitution of the circle case. A random-hemisphere sign correlation gives a meaningful geometric explanation of the universal lower bound.
